title: Media Luna to the Comandancia: Norma, the Coast, and the Packets Nobody Burned
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Doctor's House at Media Luna

stops.name: Media Luna: the doctor's daughter
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by both Wikipedias and EcuRed. The pool's coordinate, 20.1394 / -77.0928, was 35 km east of the town and has been corrected to the es.wikipedia gazetteer value for Media Luna
stops.campa: In the house Manuel Sánchez Silveira bought in 1913, in the Pueblo Nuevo quarter beside the Central Isabel mill, Acacia Manduley bears a daughter on the ninth of May. The father is physician to the mill and to the cane country around it, a reader, a liberal of the kind that will later have a party. The house is comfortable in a town where the cutters work four months of the year and eat the other eight on credit. Acacia will die while the children are still small. Whether there are eight of them or nine, the two sources do not agree.
suggested_refs: The house at Central Isabel, Pueblo Nuevo, Media Luna, bought by Dr. Manuel Sánchez Silveira in 1913

stops.name: Manzanillo: entered in the register at Vicana
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by EcuRed. The pool's Manzanillo coordinate, reused across four separate entries, was 2 km off and has been corrected to the es.wikipedia value
stops.campa: Five months after the birth the family carries the paperwork up the coast to the Juzgado Municipal de Vicana, and on the sixteenth of October the child is written into the civil register of Manzanillo. The port is the city the whole region faces: the bay, the sugar warehouses, the stevedores, the street organs built in this town and nowhere else in Cuba. Her father's patients come from both ends of the forty kilometres of cane road that separate it from Media Luna.
suggested_refs: The civil register of the Juzgado Municipal de Vicana, Manzanillo, October 1920

stops.name: Manzanillo: the font of the Purísima Concepción
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by EcuRed. The coordinate is the town centre, not the church door, which was not independently pinned
stops.campa: On the twenty-second of July 1922 she is baptized in the parish church of the Purísima Concepción, on the square at the middle of Manzanillo. She is two years old, which is late by the standards of a city parish and ordinary in the countryside of Oriente, where a christening waits on a priest, a set of godparents and a free afternoon in the dead season. After this the reachable record goes quiet: until her twentieth year it holds a register entry, a baptismal line and the name of a house.
suggested_refs: Baptismal registers of the parish of the Purísima Concepción, Manzanillo

stops.name: Pilón: the rounds
stops.date_confidence: the move is dated to about 1940 by both Wikipedias, month and day unknown, January the house default. The pool's coordinate, 19.8497 / -77.3183, fell 6 km offshore and has been corrected to the es.wikipedia value for Pilón
stops.campa: Around 1940 father and daughter move west along the coast to Pilón, under the mountains, and she keeps his house and assists his practice for the better part of sixteen years. She learns the country the way a doctor's assistant learns it: which family lives up which track, who is owed what, which river crossing floods and when. Fifteen years on, when men need hiding, she will know which houses take them in. The patients are cane cutters, charcoal burners, coffee pickers on the lower slopes of the Sierra Maestra.
suggested_refs: Dr. Manuel Sánchez Silveira's practice at Pilón, 1940 to the mid-1950s

stops.name: Manzanillo: with Chibás and the Ortodoxos
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. es.wikipedia records the Ortodoxo affiliation with no date, no document and no chapter named; 1947 is the party's founding year and January is the house default. The stop's location is inferred from where the family's political life was conducted
stops.campa: Her first politics is her father's. Manuel Sánchez Silveira is a cultured man committed to the liberal Ortodoxo party, and through him she comes to Eduardo Chibás, the radio moralist whose entire platform is the theft of public money and whose emblem is a broom. She joins. Within a few years Chibás will shoot himself at the end of a broadcast and the constitutional road he preached will be closed by an army coup. Nothing reached records when she signed on, or to which chapter.
stops.quote: Con su padre, Manuel Sánchez Silveira, médico rural, hombre culto y comprometido con el Partido Ortodoxo liberal, tuvo su primer acercamiento a la política.
suggested_refs: The Partido del Pueblo Cubano (Ortodoxo) in Oriente province under Eduardo Chibás

stops.name: Pilón: the tenth of March
stops.date_confidence: the coup is attested to the day; her whereabouts on it are not recorded, and Pilón is where she was living
stops.campa: Batista takes the government before dawn, without a shot, three months before an election he was going to lose. In Pilón the news arrives by radio like weather. Both encyclopedias that describe her say the coup is what turned her, and neither says where she was standing when she heard it, or what she said, or whom she said it to. She is thirty-one, unmarried, keeping a doctor's house in a small port at the end of a bad road. Everything she does from here on is illegal.
suggested_refs: Batista's coup of 10 March 1952 and the collapse of the Ortodoxo electoral road

stops.name: Pico Turquino: the bust carried up
stops.date_confidence: the year is agreed and the month is not: Cuban accounts variously give the centenary of Martí's birth in January and the twenty-first of May 1953. January is the house default and the disagreement stands unresolved. No primary document for the ascent was reached
stops.campa: For the centenary of José Martí's birth she organizes a climb to the summit of the highest mountain in Cuba carrying a bronze bust of him, and sets it on the peak. It is the sort of patriotic excursion respectable Cuban families made in 1953, and it is also a survey: the paths, the water, the elevation, the families who feed climbers and ask nothing. Four years later the same mountain will hide an army. The party goes up through the coffee country above Pilón with the bust roped between them.
sources: General Cuban biographical tradition, widely repeated; no primary document reached
suggested_refs: The bronze bust of José Martí at the summit of Pico Turquino, placed 1953

stops.name: Ensenada de Mora: the last holiday
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction from EcuRed, year only, January the house default. The pool's coordinate fell in open water south of the coast; this pin is the bay immediately west of Pilón and is approximate
stops.campa: She spends a holiday with her father among the small cays of the bay west of Pilón, shallow water and mangrove and white sand a few hundred metres off the coast road. It is the last stretch of ordinary family life the record preserves, and the Cuban encyclopedia gives it two lines: a country doctor and his grown daughter, out of the house, in the season when nobody in the cane country is working. The following year she is moving weapons through Manzanillo under a name that is not hers.
suggested_refs: The cays of the Ensenada de Mora, west of Pilón, Granma province

stops.name: Manzanillo: the name Norma
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested by both Wikipedias; month and day unknown, January the house default
stops.campa: She helps found the underground cell of the 26th of July Movement in the Manzanillo and Pilón district and takes the war name Norma. The work at first is arms: buying them, hiding them, carrying them through a port town thick with police. A woman of thirty-five from a respectable family, known across the district as the physician's daughter, passes checkpoints that stop any man of fighting age on sight. The movement gives her the district for that reason.
stops.quote: ...si esa mujer es como tú dices, donde mejor está es en Manzanillo, porque allí va a ser más útil...
stops.quote_source: Fidel Castro, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Celia Sánchez Manduley', on assigning her to organize in Manzanillo; the source itself prints the remark with ellipses
suggested_refs: The Manzanillo cell of the Movimiento 26 de Julio, 1955-1956

stops.name: El Marabuzal: the first detachment goes up
stops.date_confidence: es.wikipedia dates the dispatch to the 1956-1957 window without a day; January 1956 is the house default. The farm itself is not independently pinned and the coordinate is Manzanillo town
stops.campa: From a farm outside Manzanillo called El Marabuzal her network assembles and sends up the first armed detachment to reinforce the guerrillas in the mountains. It is one of several dozen such places in the district whose names survive only because something left from them. Men are gathered in ones and twos on ordinary pretexts, fed, armed out of the caches and walked out at night toward the foothills. The Spanish record names the farm and nothing else about it: no owner, no house, no road.
suggested_refs: The farm of El Marabuzal, Manzanillo district

stops.name: Niquero: the trucks that wait
stops.date_confidence: the preparations are attested for 1956 without a day; the thirtieth of November is the date the landing was expected and the rising in Santiago was timed to, and is used as the reference point rather than as an attested day in her own movements
stops.campa: Along the coast west of Media Luna she stages the reception: trucks, drivers, guides, food, and men who know the mangrove, held ready in and around Niquero for a boat expected from Mexico. The caches are laid in advance, rifles and cartridges and medicine distributed through houses whose owners are told only what they must move and on what night. Frank País has the urban movement rising in Santiago on the thirtieth to pull the army the other way. Everything depends on the boat arriving on the thirtieth.
stops.quote: Por orientaciones del Movimiento organizó una red de colaboradores campesinos en las cercanías de donde debía desembarcar la expedición dirigida por Fidel Castro.
stops.quote_source: es.wikipedia, 'Celia Sánchez Manduley', on her preparations for the Granma landing
sources: Hugh Thomas, Cuba: The Pursuit of Freedom (cited by the research pool, not consulted directly)
suggested_refs: Niquero and the coastal staging of the Granma reception, November 1956

stops.name: Playa Las Coloradas: two days late
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The coordinate is inherited byte-identical from fidel_castro.journey.json, whose own note records it as approximate; the boat in fact grounded at Los Cayuelos, about 2 km from the beach, per es.wikipedia 'Desembarco del Granma' and EcuRed
stops.campa: The Granma is two days behind schedule, out of fuel and off course, and grounds not on the beach but at Los Cayuelos, a mangrove point about two kilometres from it. Eighty-two men wade ashore into swamp, leaving most of the heavy equipment in the boat. The rising in Santiago has already come and gone; the army is awake and the coast is watched. Her trucks, her drivers and the men who know the mangrove are somewhere along this shore, and the meeting never happens.
suggested_refs: Los Cayuelos and the Portada de la Libertad, Parque Nacional Desembarco del Granma

stops.name: Manzanillo: word of the ambush in the cane
stops.date_confidence: the ambush at Alegría de Pío is attested to the day; her own whereabouts that week are recorded nowhere reached, and Manzanillo is where her network was based. This stop is not staged at the ambush site, where she was not present
stops.campa: Three days after the landing the army catches the column in a canefield at Alegría de Pío and scatters it. Where she is that week nothing records. She is somewhere in the Manzanillo district with a network of peasant houses built to receive a landing that has already failed, and the network now has a different job: find whoever is still alive, hide them, feed them, move them east into the mountains without being seen. Of eighty-two men who came ashore, the number that will reassemble is closer to twenty.
stops.quote: Following the disastrous landing of the Granma in 1956, Sánchez organised the peasant family network which housed and fed the rebels.
suggested_refs: The peasant support network of the Manzanillo and Niquero coast, December 1956

stops.name: Campechuela: the rifles along the coast
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The coastal arms chain through Campechuela is regional tradition with no document reached; the day is a placeholder within the weeks after the landing, when the survivors in the Sierra had more men than weapons
stops.campa: Rifles move up the coast road through Campechuela, a sugar port between Manzanillo and Media Luna, in the months when the survivors in the mountains have more men than weapons and no way to buy any. Everything comes through hands: a shotgun bought from a farmer, a pistol lifted from a barracks, ammunition counted out in coffee sacks by people who will be shot if it is found on them. The attribution of this particular town to her network rests on regional tradition rather than on any document reached. Arms reach the Sierra from this coast, and she is the one moving them.
sources: Regional Cuban Revolution historiography, uncited in the research pool
suggested_refs: The coastal arms-distribution chain between Campechuela and the Sierra Maestra, 1957

stops.name: Purial de Vicana: the first climb
stops.date_confidence: EcuRed records a February 1957 ascent with Frank País; es.wikipedia states her first ascent was 19 March. Both cannot be first and neither source acknowledges the other. Day unknown, first of the month the house default. The coordinate is EcuRed's for Purial de Vicana, the foothill zone through which the mountains were reached, and is approximate for the meeting itself
stops.campa: In February she goes up into the foothills with Frank País to meet the column and settle what it needs. Spanish Wikipedia says her first ascent was the nineteenth of March; the Cuban encyclopedia records this earlier climb with País. Both cannot be the first, and neither source mentions the other's date. What the two agree on is the content of the work: count the men, list what is missing, fix which houses in the Purial country will carry a message and which will not.
suggested_refs: Frank País and the coordination between the llano and the Sierra, early 1957

stops.name: Sierra Maestra: the nineteenth of March
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by es.wikipedia, which calls it her ascent to the Sierra; see the February stop for the contradiction. The coordinate is a general pin for the mountain theatre, no camp being specified
stops.campa: On the nineteenth of March she goes up again, and this is the date the Spanish record keeps. She does not stop being the coast. For the rest of the war she moves between the mountain camp and the towns below it, carrying up what a mountain camp cannot make and carrying down what only she can be trusted with. Messages go out in her hand, some of them, the story runs, folded inside flowers. The column at this point is a few dozen men who have won one small fight.
stops.quote: En cuanto a la Sierra, cuando se escriba la historia de esta etapa revolucionaria, en la portada tendrán que aparecer dos nombres: David y Norma.
stops.quote_source: Letter from the guerrilleros of the Sierra Maestra to Frank País, 1957, quoted in es.wikipedia and EcuRed; David was País's clandestine name, Norma was hers
suggested_refs: The courier and supply line between Manzanillo and the rebel column, 1957

stops.name: El Uvero: the garrison on the shore
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by EcuRed. The pool's coordinate put El Uvero in the wrong province, near Pilón in Granma; EcuRed places it in the municipality of Guamá, Santiago de Cuba, on the south coast near Chivirico. This pin is derived from that coastal strip and is approximate to within a few kilometres
stops.campa: The rebels come down out of the mountains before dawn onto the army post at El Uvero, on the south coast in the Guamá country, and take it in something under three hours of close fighting. Both sides lose dead and wounded, and the column spends the days after the attack carrying its own casualties back inland. Celia Sánchez is in it. The standard Cuban account makes her the first woman to hold a combat position in the ranks of the Rebel Army, and dates the fact to this morning, the twenty-eighth of May 1957.
suggested_refs: The combat of El Uvero, 28 May 1957, and the army post on the Guamá coast

stops.name: Sierra Maestra: the star of the Comandante
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the coordinate is inherited byte-identical from che_guevara.journey.json, which names Celia Sánchez at this stop
stops.campa: Fidel Castro makes the Argentine doctor the first comandante of the column, a rank until this day his own and nobody else's, and it is Celia Sánchez who pins the star to Che Guevara's beret. The promotion arrives inside a letter written about other business, a line near the bottom of a page. There is no ceremony beyond the act: a small metal star, a wool beret, a clearing in the woods, a handful of men watching from wherever they happen to be sitting. She keeps the letter. She keeps all of them.
suggested_refs: Fidel Castro's letter of 21 July 1957 naming Guevara comandante, held in the Oficina de Asuntos Históricos

stops.name: Sierra Maestra: the packets
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. No source consulted dates or describes a wartime practice of preserving papers; it is inferred backward from the archive director's 2014 statement that the Sierra documents reached her apartment still in the packets prepared during the war. The date is a placeholder inside that window
stops.campa: In a guerrilla camp paper is fuel and cigarette wrapping. She refuses to let it be. Orders, letters, receipts, photographs, the scraps on which a war conducts its ordinary business, get gathered and wrapped and set aside instead of burned. Fifty-seven years later the director of the archive she will found describes the Sierra documents arriving at her Havana flat still in the same packets prepared during the war. That the habit began here in the mountains is an inference from that one sentence. No source consulted watches her do it, or says who told her to.
sources: es.wikipedia, 'Celia Sánchez Manduley', citation 10 (Eugenio Suárez Pérez, 2014)
suggested_refs: The wartime packets of Sierra Maestra documents, founding core of the fondo de Celia

stops.name: La Comandancia de La Plata: the houses in the trees
stops.date_confidence: the headquarters is attested for the war's last year but not to a founding day; January is the house default, and EcuRed dates its establishment to May 1958. The coordinate is inherited byte-identical from fidel_castro.journey.json for the same site, though EcuRed places the Comandancia in Bartolomé Masó on the northern slope, which suggests a pin nearer 20.02 / -76.94; the discrepancy affects both files and should be fixed in both at once
stops.campa: The command post above the La Plata river becomes a small state under the canopy: hospital, press, and from February the transmitter of Radio Rebelde. She conceives the buildings, and the Cuban record is exact about the terms she set. Not one tree felled. No ground levelled. Every house fitted to the slope it stands on, so that nothing shows from the air. She sees to the blankets and to the flowers. The archive's own phrase for the rest of it is details of beauty and sensitivity.
suggested_refs: La Comandancia General de La Plata, national monument, Sierra Maestra

stops.name: Pino del Agua: the running fight
stops.date_confidence: EcuRed attests her presence at the operations of 16 February 1958; the coordinate for Pino del Agua is approximate
stops.campa: She is present for the operations around Pino del Agua on the sixteenth of February 1958. What she does there the Cuban encyclopedia does not say. It records that she was there, in a list of dates, between two other dates, and moves on without a further word. This is the pine country in the high Sierra where the rebels ambush an army column twice in four months on the same stretch of road, in September of 1957 and again now. She is dated to the second of the two.
suggested_refs: The two combats at Pino del Agua, September 1957 and February 1958

stops.name: Bartolomé Masó: the road into the mountains
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, dated to the 1957-1958 window without a day; May is a placeholder. The coordinate is the pool's district-level pin and sits some 7 km northwest of the town proper
stops.campa: The town at the foot of the range is a hinge in the supply line: what is bought in Manzanillo comes this far by road and goes on by mule. Boots, salt, batteries, iodine, rifle ammunition packed in coffee sacks, and the newsprint and ink for a press in the mountains. The attribution of the route to her network is regional tradition and not document; nothing reached names her at Bartolomé Masó. The traffic itself runs for months, and nobody is caught on it.
sources: Regional Cuban Revolution historiography, uncited in the research pool
suggested_refs: The Manzanillo to Bartolomé Masó supply road and the mule tracks above it

stops.name: El Jigüe: the summer offensive
stops.date_confidence: EcuRed dates the battle 11 to 21 July 1958 and places it near the confluence of the Jigüe and La Plata streams by Arroyo de las Cuevas, in present-day Guamá, on the southern slope; the pool's date and its northern-slope coordinate have both been corrected, and this pin remains approximate
stops.campa: From the eleventh to the twenty-first of July an army battalion is surrounded and broken near where the Jigüe stream runs into the La Plata, and Batista's summer offensive turns there. Cuban tradition puts Celia Sánchez behind the fight, moving supplies up and getting the wounded out. The encyclopedia entry on the battle itself does not mention her anywhere. Whether she was near the Jigüe in those ten days, and who first said that she was, is not recorded.
sources: General Cuban Revolution historiography, for her role
suggested_refs: The battle of El Jigüe, 11-21 July 1958, and the surrender of Major Quevedo's battalion

stops.name: La Plata: the Mariana Grajales platoon
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by es.wikipedia; the coordinate is the Comandancia pin, inherited from fidel_castro.journey.json
stops.campa: On the fourth of September the all-woman platoon is formed at the command post, over the objection of men in the column who do not want to hand rifles to it. Celia Sánchez helps organize it; Fidel Castro arms it and teaches it to shoot. It takes the name of Mariana Grajales, mother of the Maceo brothers, who gave her sons to the first war of independence and outlived most of them. Teté Puebla is seventeen years old and in it, and what she remembers is Fidel Castro teaching them to shoot and naming them his personal escort.
stops.quote: Como muchos hombres no nos tenían confianza, Fidel no solo fue quien nos enseñó a disparar sino que nos nombró su escolta personal. Por eso, cuando íbamos llegando a los lugares, la gente decía: ¿Llegaron las Marianas? ¡Seguro detrás viene Fidel!
stops.quote_source: Delsa Esther 'Teté' Puebla, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Celia Sánchez Manduley', citation 7
suggested_refs: The Pelotón Femenino Mariana Grajales, formed at La Plata, 4 September 1958

stops.name: Havana: the caravan arrives
stops.date_confidence: the caravan's entry into Havana is attested to 8 January 1959; her presence in it is attested by Puebla's testimony without a day of its own
stops.campa: The column comes west across the whole island in eight days, town by town, stopping wherever a crowd forms across the road, and enters Havana on the eighth of January. She is in it. Teté Puebla, riding in the same caravan, remembers her scarcely resting, attending to the Marianas, to the soldiers, to children found along the road and above all to Fidel Castro. She is thirty-eight years old, and will live in this city for the remaining twenty-one years of her life.
stops.quote: Nada he olvidado. Recuerdo en la Caravana que Celia, igual que en la Sierra, apenas descansaba para estar siempre pendiente de todo. Ella era así. No tenía descanso. Estaba al tanto del último detalle de lo que necesitábamos las Marianas, los soldados del Ejército Rebelde, los niños que encontraba y, sobre todo, de lo que necesitaba Fidel.
stops.quote_source: Delsa Esther 'Teté' Puebla on the Caravana de la Libertad, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Celia Sánchez Manduley', citation 7
suggested_refs: The Caravana de la Libertad, Santiago to Havana, 1-8 January 1959

stops.name: Habana Libre: the twenty-third floor
stops.date_confidence: the date and the room are attested for Castro; her presence in that lobby is standard biography and is not stated in any document reached. The coordinate is inherited byte-identical from fidel_castro.journey.json
stops.campa: For three months the government of Cuba runs out of a hotel. Fidel Castro takes room 2324 of what was the Hilton until the revolution took it, and the lobby below fills with petitioners, journalists, foreign visitors and armed men from the mountains. Somebody has to decide who goes up. From here on, that somebody is her. Her biographers put the beginning of her later office in these months. No decree appoints her to it, and no minute records the arrangement being made.
suggested_refs: The Habana Libre, room 2324, seat of government January to March 1959

stops.name: Vedado: the apartment on Calle 11
stops.date_confidence: es.wikipedia dates the accumulation to the first years of the 1960s without a day; January 1960 is the house default. The address, Calle 11 between 10 and 12, is attested; the coordinate is derived from the Vedado street grid and is not gazetteered. The pool's pin was the district centroid, 1.3 km east
stops.campa: From the first years of the sixties the documents pile up in her flat on Calle 11 between Calles 10 and 12. The Sierra papers are still in their wartime wrapping. The rest she gets out of surviving fighters and out of the families of the dead by her own asking, and it comes in loose and goes into big canvas sacks. Nobody has given her the job and nothing authorizes it. What is in the flat is the only full record of how the government she works for came to exist.
stops.quote: Ella estuvo todo el tiempo pendiente de la historia de Fidel y de los revolucionarios en la Sierra y luego del triunfo. Desde los primeros años de la década de 1960 comenzó a acumular los documentos en su apartamento de la calle 11 entre 10 y 12 del Vedado. Los de la Sierra guardados en los mismos paquetes preparados durante la guerra; y los otros, conseguidos como resultado de sus gestiones con combatientes y familiares de los mártires después del triunfo, se depositaron en grandes bolsas de lona.
stops.quote_source: Eugenio Suárez Pérez, director of the Oficina de Asuntos Históricos, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Celia Sánchez Manduley' (2014), citation 10
suggested_refs: The flat at Calle 11 entre 10 y 12, Vedado, first home of the fondo de Celia

stops.name: Plaza de la Revolución: Secretary of the Presidency
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by es.wikipedia. The location is inferred: no source consulted sites her office at the Palacio de la Revolución. The pool's gloss that she held the post 'for over twenty years' is wrong; from March 1962 to January 1980 is under eighteen
stops.campa: On the twenty-third of March she is made Secretary of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, and she holds the post until she dies. After the constitution of 1976 the same office is called the Secretariat of the Council of State. What the title covers is what she has been doing since the hotel: the diary, the correspondence, the visitors, the filter through which anything reaching Fidel Castro has to pass. Where her desk actually stood is not stated in anything reached.
suggested_refs: The Secretariat of the Council of Ministers, later of the Council of State, 1962-1980

stops.name: Vedado: the Office of Historical Affairs
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by EcuRed, on her initiative. The pool duplicated her flat's coordinate; EcuRed gives the office at Calle 8 No. 210 between 11 and Línea, and this pin is derived from that grid address. The institution's name is anachronistic for 1964, the Council of State dating only from 1976
stops.campa: On the fourth of May the private accumulation becomes an institution, at her initiative, in a house on Calle 8 a few blocks from her own. It will hold more than fifty-six thousand documents and over a hundred and fifty-nine thousand photographs in twenty-eight collections, and the people who work there call the founding core el fondo de Celia. The name the office carries, Office of Historical Affairs of the Council of State, is an anachronism: there is no Council of State in Cuba in 1964, and will not be for another twelve years.
sources: EcuRed, 'Oficina de Asuntos Históricos del Consejo de Estado'
suggested_refs: The Oficina de Asuntos Históricos, Calle 8 No. 210, Vedado, founded 4 May 1964

stops.name: Coppelia: the name of a ballet
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by en.wikipedia. The pool credited her with championing the project; en.wikipedia credits the project to Fidel Castro and the building to the architect Mario Girona, and credits her only with the name. The coordinate has been corrected 380 m north to the La Rampa block
stops.campa: The ice-cream park opens on the fourth of June on La Rampa, Mario Girona's concrete flower on stilts, standing in its own garden on a block where a hospital had been. The project belongs to Fidel Castro; the building belongs to Girona. The name belongs to her: she calls it Coppelia, after her favourite ballet, and it sticks so hard that Havana stops remembering the block was ever anything else. Twenty-six flavours to begin with, served in the open air, in a country deep into a rationing system, to anybody willing to stand in the queue.
suggested_refs: Coppelia, La Rampa, Vedado, opened 4 June 1966, architect Mario Girona

stops.name: Granma: the women who had fought
stops.date_confidence: EcuRed attests the visit to the day; the newspaper's building near the Plaza de la Revolución was not gazetteered and the pool's coordinate did not match it, so this pin is approximate
stops.campa: She goes to the offices of the party newspaper with women who had been combatants in the Sierra, nine years after the platoon was formed. It belongs to the same habit as the packets and the canvas sacks: get the survivors into one room, on a fixed date, in front of somebody whose job is to write things down. The visit survives as a single line in a Cuban encyclopedia entry, with no result given, no purpose stated and no list of who went with her.
suggested_refs: The offices of the newspaper Granma, Plaza de la Revolución, Havana

stops.name: Parque Lenin: the park south of the city
stops.date_confidence: the inauguration is attested to the day by es.wikipedia, which credits the design to Antonio Quintana Simonetti and does not mention her at all; her role as promoter is Cuban memory rather than sourced record and is tagged as reconstruction. The pool's coordinate was 2 km off and has been corrected
stops.campa: A park of some seven hundred hectares opens south of the city on the twenty-second of April, with a lake, an amphitheatre, a narrow-gauge railway and an aquarium for freshwater fish. The design is Antonio Quintana Simonetti's, and the Spanish record of the park does not mention her anywhere in it. Cuban memory is nonetheless unanimous that the place exists because she pushed it through. She is credited the same way with a run of public works in these years, driven past ministries that had other priorities.
sources: General Cuban historiography, for her role as promoter
suggested_refs: Parque Lenin, inaugurated 22 April 1972, architect Antonio Quintana Simonetti

stops.name: Vedado: the question nobody answers
stops.date_confidence: no date attaches to this at all; the stop is placed late in the Havana years, at her own address, and the year is a bare placeholder. The two source traditions are irreconcilable and are both reported
stops.campa: For twenty years she is the person nearest the head of the Cuban state, and for twenty years the question of what that means is asked everywhere except on the record. Outside Cuba the rumour makes them lovers and the biographies keep the question open. Cuban accounts describe a political partnership of a singular kind and take care to say it is not a marriage. Neither of them ever addressed it in public, in either direction, and neither denied it. She never married and left no children.
stops.quote: Speculation over the intimacy of Celia Sánchez and Fidel Castro's relationship is subject to debate, including rumours of the two sharing a romantic relationship. However, neither Sánchez nor Castro addressed these rumours during their lifetime.
sources: Georgie Anne Geyer, Guerrilla Prince, and Nancy Stout, One Day in December (named by the research pool, neither consulted)
BBC Mundo, on the question of whether she was Castro's lover (fetch blocked this session)
suggested_refs: Nancy Stout, One Day in December: Celia Sánchez and the Cuban Revolution (2013)

stops.name: Havana: the eleventh of January
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by both Wikipedias. No hospital or clinic is named in any source consulted. The pool's addition that she had been diagnosed less than a year earlier appears in neither article and has been dropped as unsourced
stops.campa: She dies of lung cancer at fifty-nine. Which hospital, no source consulted says. The country is going into a bad decade: the rationing tightening, the Mariel exodus three months ahead, the war in Angola in its fifth year. Twenty-three years earlier she had walked up into the Sierra Maestra with a list of what a column of eighty men was missing, and from that March to this January she was never once out of the work. Fidel Castro calls her a symbol to the Revolution.
stops.quote: I truly believe that this is the best form of tribute to pay to someone who dedicated herself to duty, without resting for a moment, without forgetting one single detail; and I believe, sincerely, that this is the most heartfelt, profound and revolutionary homage that one can give to a compatriot who gave her life for the Revolution.
stops.quote_source: Fidel Castro, speech at the dedication of the hospital named for Celia Sánchez, 16 January 1981, English translation quoted at en.wikipedia, 'Celia Sánchez', citation 19
suggested_refs: Fidel Castro's dedication speech at the hospital named for Celia Sánchez, January 1981

stops.name: Necrópolis de Cristóbal Colón: a contested grave
stops.date_confidence: the burial is dated to January 1980 without a day; the thirteenth is a placeholder two days after the death. The place is contested, see the campa. Three different coordinates for the cemetery appeared in the research pool and this one is en.wikipedia's
stops.campa: The Spanish record says she was buried in the Colón cemetery. The English record says a memorial and a mausoleum for her were built in Parque Lenin, the park she is credited with making, and that her remains lie now at Colón. The English article on the cemetery itself does not list her among its notable dead. Three separate sets of coordinates for the grave are in circulation. No source reached settles which of them is the grave, or whether the remains were moved from Parque Lenin at all.
suggested_refs: The mausoleum and memorial to Celia Sánchez in Parque Lenin, Havana

stops.name: Media Luna: the house opened
stops.date_confidence: contested. EcuRed dates the museum's inauguration to 11 January 1983, the third anniversary of her death, and the declaration of the house as a national monument to 1990; es.wikipedia dates the opening to 9 May 1990, which would have been her seventieth birthday and may conflate the two events. EcuRed's date is used and the disagreement stands
stops.campa: The house where she was born, at number 111 of the avenue now named for Raúl Podio Saborit, is opened to the public. The Cuban encyclopedia dates the opening to the third anniversary of her death and the declaration of the house as a national monument to 1990; the Spanish encyclopedia dates the opening itself to 1990, on what would have been her seventieth birthday. A hundred and forty-four objects are shown in the rooms she grew up in, among them a Colt .45, a Springfield rifle and an M-1 carbine.
sources: EcuRed, 'Museo Casa Natal Celia Sánchez Manduley'
suggested_refs: Museo Casa Natal Celia Sánchez Manduley, Ave. Raúl Podio Saborit 111, Media Luna

stops.name: Manzanillo: the altar and the monument
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction throughout. The memorial is undated in every source reached and the year is a bare placeholder after her death; the substance of the claim is itself contested, see the campa
stops.campa: In the port city she worked out of there is a memorial and, by one account, a mausoleum. There is also a sentence in the English record about the people of Manzanillo using an altar of the Virgen de la Caridad del Cobre as a marriage altar, tied to her dedication to the revolution and explained no further than that. Repeated onward, this has turned into a tiled staircase on the seafront where couples are photographed on their wedding day. Nothing reached supports that version, and nothing reached clearly supports any other.
suggested_refs: The ceramic monument to Celia Sánchez at Manzanillo, and the altar of the Virgen de la Caridad del Cobre

stops.name: Havana: the watermark
stops.date_confidence: en.wikipedia dates the coin to ten years after her death, that is 1990, without a day; January is the house default. None of the numismatic detail was checked against a catalogue
stops.campa: Ten years after her death a ten-peso coin is struck with her face on it. Her portrait is also worked into the watermark of several varieties of Cuban banknote, which is to say that for decades Cubans have been holding her up to the light to see whether the money is real. Schools, hospitals and community centres carry her name, in Cuba and as far away as Zimbabwe. The English source that carries all of this is thin, and none of it has been checked against a numismatic catalogue.
suggested_refs: The Cuban 10-peso coin of 1990 and the Celia Sánchez watermark on Cuban banknotes
